canonical.name: Finite-dimensional Heisenberg central extension and exponentiated Weyl C*-algebra
Finite-dimensional Stone–von Neumann uniqueness at a fixed nonzero central character
Boundary examples for zero character, nonregular representations and infinitely many modes
canonical.reason: The separate B-page items prove each boundary directly and remain outside the A-page theorem chain.

sources.title: Roland Speicher, Mathematical Aspects of Quantum Mechanics, Lecture Notes
sources.locator: Example VII.3 and Proposition VII.6, PDF pp. 39–41; Definition VII.5, PDF pp. 40–41; Theorem VIII.1 and proof, Remarks VIII.5–VIII.6, PDF pp. 43–47; Chapter X, §§X.1–X.2, PDF pp. 54–58.
sources.source_kind_detail: Complete author-hosted university lecture-notes PDF; the cited portions were inspected in the complete extracted source text.

contents.name: Example VII.3: Schrödinger representation
contents.support: Gives the one-mode translation and modulation model; the local lemma verifies its finite-dimensional formula and irreducibility directly.

contents.name: Definition VII.5: strongly continuous representations of the Weyl relations
contents.support: Supports the regularity and irreducibility vocabulary; the local definition states the vector-space phase convention.

contents.name: Proposition VII.6: irreducibility of the Schrödinger Weyl representation
contents.support: An independent one-mode irreducibility treatment; the local proof supplies the all-n Fourier and Tonelli argument.

contents.name: Theorem VIII.1: uniqueness theorem for the Weyl relations
contents.support: Supports the fixed nonzero central-character uniqueness claim; the source proof is one-mode and the local proof supplies the complete finite-dimensional Mackey argument.

contents.name: Remark VIII.5: Gaussian Weyl average projects onto the vacuum
contents.support: Motivates the Gaussian average; the local proof computes its kernel for every positive width a.

contents.name: Remark VIII.6(ii): infinite degrees of freedom do not satisfy the finite uniqueness theorem
contents.support: States the infinite-mode boundary; the local example constructs and separates two concrete irreducible regular systems.

contents.name: Definition X.1 and Remark X.2: incomplete tensor products and finite-coordinate embeddings
contents.support: Supplies the reference-vector construction and embeddings; the local definition verifies its specific L² isometries and rank-one coordinate projections.

contents.name: Theorem X.3: equivalence criterion for reference-vector tensor products
contents.reason: The source gives only a sketch of its equivalence criterion, and the counterexample proves inequivalence directly by a local projection expectation limit without invoking that criterion.

contents.name: Example X.4: inequivalent representations of CCR(∞)
contents.support: The source example motivates the infinite-mode boundary but sketches its separation argument; the local proof supplies cyclicity, irreducibility and inequivalence in full.

read_evidence.access_method: Inspected the complete author-hosted PDF through its extracted full-text copy, checking every cited section and proof passage.
read_evidence.extent: Read Example VII.3, the Weyl-relation discussion and Proposition VII.6; the full statement/proof of Theorem VIII.1 and Remarks VIII.5–VIII.6; and Chapter X Definition X.1, Remark X.2, Theorem X.3 and Example X.4. The text says the finite multi-mode extension is similar and labels the infinite-product inequivalence proof a sketch; neither omitted proof is imported.

sources.title: Amritanshu Prasad, An Easy Proof of the Stone-von Neumann-Mackey Theorem
sources.locator: §4.1, theorem statement, PDF pp. 4–5; §4.3, real-vector-space proof, PDF pp. 6–9.
sources.source_kind_detail: Complete author-posted arXiv paper PDF, downloaded and inspected at the full cited sections.

contents.name: Theorem (Stone-von Neumann-Mackey), §4.1
contents.support: States irreducibility of the canonical model and uniqueness for fixed central character; the local theorem uses an independent spectral-measure and imprimitivity proof.

contents.name: §4.3 Weyl operators and the Fourier-Wigner transform
contents.support: Provides an independent formula and phase convention for the canonical Weyl operators.

contents.name: Equation (4.2): isometry of the Fourier-Wigner transform
contents.reason: The current theorem uses Mackey imprimitivity rather than the Fourier-Wigner transform; no claim depends on this isometry or its Plancherel proof.

contents.name: §4.3 proof of irreducibility of the canonical representation
contents.support: The source proves irreducibility by Fourier-Wigner orthogonality; the local proof uses Fourier uniqueness and Tonelli instead.

contents.name: Lemma 4.1: injectivity of the integrated Weyl transform
contents.reason: The integrated-transform injectivity lemma is not a premise of the local universal C*-completion or Mackey proof.

contents.name: Lemma 4.2: a Fourier-Wigner coefficient gives a rank-one operator
contents.support: Supplies an independent rank-one averaging identity; the local lemma computes the weighted integral kernel directly for all a>0.

contents.name: §4.3 Gaussian projection and uniqueness argument
contents.support: The Gaussian average motivates the helper; the local item verifies normalization, projection, intertwiners and totality.

contents.name: §4.4 passage to general locally compact abelian groups
contents.reason: The assigned theorem is limited to finite-dimensional real symplectic spaces, so the broader locally compact abelian group extension is outside its statement.

read_evidence.access_method: Downloaded the complete arXiv PDF, extracted its text locally, and inspected the full §4.1 and §4.3 proofs.
read_evidence.extent: Read the full theorem statement, all of §4.3 including the Weyl transform, Lemmas 4.1 and 4.2, the Gaussian projection, and the uniqueness argument. The compressed Fourier inversion and Plancherel transitions are not used as missing steps in the local arguments.

sources.title: Christopher J. Fewster and Kasia Rejzner, Algebraic Quantum Field Theory—an introduction, arXiv:1904.04051v2
sources.locator: §4, “Weyl algebra”, PDF pp. 17–18, including Exercises 14–17 and the explicit ℓ²(S) construction.
sources.source_kind_detail: Complete author-posted arXiv v2 PDF, extracted and read at the cited Weyl-algebra section.

contents.name: §4 Weyl algebra: Weyl *-relations and C*-completion
contents.support: Gives the bounded Weyl-symbol relations and states uniqueness of the C*-completion with an external citation; the local proof constructs the universal seminorm and completion.

contents.name: Exercise 14: prove W(0)=1
contents.support: The local cocycle and unit calculation proves the algebraic identity directly.

contents.name: Equation (34): explicit ℓ²(S) Weyl representation
contents.support: Provides the twisted left-regular construction; the local counterexample verifies the product, adjoint, universal extension and discontinuity.

contents.name: Exercises 15–16: Weyl adjoints, products and norm discontinuity
contents.support: The product and inverse are verified locally, and a basis-vector calculation proves strong discontinuity.

contents.name: Unbounded field operators cannot be recovered by differentiating inside the Weyl C*-algebra
contents.support: Supports the local separation between bounded Weyl symbols and unbounded field operators; no domain-free commutator is asserted.

contents.name: Exercise 17: tracial GNS realization of the left-regular representation
contents.reason: The example needs only the directly constructed Hilbert-space *-representation and its nonregularity, not the tracial-state GNS identification.

read_evidence.access_method: Inspected the complete arXiv v2 PDF through its extracted full-text copy at the cited Weyl-algebra section.
read_evidence.extent: Read the full Weyl-algebra subsection on PDF pages 17–18, including the defining relations, completion statement, explicit representation (34), Exercises 14–17 and the paragraph on unbounded fields. The source cites rather than proves the completion theorem and leaves W(0)=1 as an exercise; the local algebra lemma supplies its own proof.

canonical.name: Zero central parameter admits inequivalent regular characters
The discrete universal Weyl algebra has nonregular representations
Infinite-mode regular representations need not be equivalent
